description: AGSC-11-24: a translation-layer peer needs a crosswalk, and a result whose IRI is the object of several statements carries one crosswalk object for each, in code-point order of local. Derivation: a.example keeps its own model and translates b.example's through domain/b.ttl, which holds two statements about https://b.example/concepts/client/: a.example's customer is skos:broadMatch to it (the peer's concept is broader) and a.example's account-holder is skos:closeMatch to it. The result for that IRI carries both objects in code-point order of local, so account-holder (a) comes before customer (c). The relationship is translation-layer and the result stays untrusted with its origin; the crosswalk makes it neither trusted nor a Link.
